items.title: From Words to Worlds: Integrating MCP into the Unreal Editor | Unreal Fest Chicago 2026
items.excerpt: Unreal Engine 5.8 ships an official Model Context Protocol integration plus new PCG spatial primitives, letting models like Claude operate inside the editor on Blueprints, levels, materials and meshes while everything stays editable.
items.rationale: An official MCP surface inside the Unreal Editor is the single most actionable item in the pool — it turns agent-driven level, material and Blueprint work into a supported workflow rather than a hack.

items.title: NVIDIA releases its RTX Neural Texture Compression SDK for the ARM64 platform
items.excerpt: NVIDIA shipped its RTX Neural Texture Compression SDK for ARM64 ahead of RTX Spark laptops, letting developers keep high-res texture detail at a fraction of the VRAM. Neural asset compression moves into shipping art pipelines.
items.rationale: Neural compression stops being a demo and becomes a shipping SDK: texture artists can budget for higher-res source detail without paying the usual VRAM tax.

items.title: Ethical Usage of Image and Video Models to Accelerate Workflows | Unreal Fest Chicago 2026
items.excerpt: An Unreal Fest Chicago 2026 session on folding Tripo 3.1, Nano Banana and ChatGPT Images 2.0 into an art production pipeline without wrecking authorship. A practical ethics-plus-workflow talk for game art teams.
items.rationale: Names the actual tools and the guardrails around them, so an art lead can copy the pipeline and the disclosure policy at the same time.

items.title: Opening Unity to everyone - one API, every role
items.excerpt: Unity is opening the Editor beyond the Editor: one API and a set of services so every role — and every agent or script — can drive the same project surface. Groundwork for AI-assisted pipelines around Unity 7.
items.rationale: The Unity-side counterpart to Unreal's MCP move: a single API surface every role or agent can drive, which is how non-engineers get automated pipelines without engine plugins.

items.title: Google AI leaks "scarily accurate and very specific" game detail from private documents, says indie dev
items.excerpt: An indie dev says Google's AI surfaced an unannounced project name that existed only in their private documents. A hard question for any studio piping design docs through cloud AI tooling.
items.rationale: The freshest item and the one that changes behaviour tomorrow: unannounced project details leaking out of private docs is a direct argument for auditing which AI tools touch your design bible.
